article_content: The former PM has called Gaza 'a prison camp' and advocated for a two-state solution, but he is also a staunch backer of Israel. The unexpected return of former United Kingdom Prime Minister David Cameron to British politics during Israel's war in Gaza and pro-Palestinian protests in Britain has sparked questions over the implications for the UK's policies towards the Middle East. Cameron, now foreign secretary, has previously called the Gaza Strip 'a prison camp' and advocated for a two-state solution to the Israel-Palestine conflict, but he has also been a staunch backer of Israel. On October 9, 2023, as Israel announced a 'total' blockade on Gaza and pummelled the enclave in retaliation for a surprise attack two days earlier by the armed Palestinian group Hamas, the 57-year-old made his pronouncement in favour of Israel. 'I stand in complete solidarity with Israel at this most challenging time and fully back the Prime Minister and UK Government in their unequivocal and steadfast support,' he said on X, including the blue and white Israeli flag in his post. 'My thoughts and prayers go out to the people of Israel following the despicable acts of terror brought upon them over the weekend, and my heart goes out to all those who have so cruelly been taken against their will, and their families. Their worry and heartache is simply...' pic.twitter.com/yFkRIorHjs — David Cameron (@David_Cameron) October 9, 2023. Hundreds of thousands of protesters have marched in London in solidarity with Palestinians in Gaza over the weekend as a small number of far-right groups staged counterprotests. Prime Minister Rishi Sunak sacked Home Secretary Suella Braverman on Monday after she drew anger for accusing police of being too lenient with pro-Palestinian protesters and making comments described as 'inflammatory'. He replaced Braverman with Foreign Secretary James Cleverly before announcing Cameron as Cleverly's surprise replacement. Ben Whitham, professor of international relations at the School of Oriental and African Studies in London (SOAS), said that while Cameron was expected to strike 'a more conciliatory tone', he would not be favourable to Palestinians in the conflict. 'Certainly, like any senior Conservative politician, he is broadly going to side with Israel and its alleged right to carry out the offensive in Gaza,' he told Al Jazeera. Whitham said Cameron's appointment was also aimed at 'healing some of the divisions within the Conservative Party'. 'He is seen as having strong ties to strategic economic partners in the Middle East,' including an ongoing personal relationship with Saudi Arabia's leadership, Whitham said. During his tenure as prime minister from 2010 to 2016, Cameron criticised Israel's 'illegal' settlements in the occupied West Bank and the blockade of the Gaza Strip. 'Gaza cannot and must not be allowed to remain a prison camp,' he said on a visit to Turkey in 2010. However, as Palestinians in Gaza benefitted from a fleeting ceasefire that temporarily halted one of the deadliest bombardments in the enclave in 2014, his party rejected calls from coalition members to re-examine arms export licenses to Israel should the fighting resume. Israeli newspaper Haaretz cited the episode among the reasons why Cameron was the most pro-Israeli British prime minister ever, snatching the honorific title from 'ardent' supporters like Gordon Brown and Tony Blair and 'unabashed admirers of the Zionist endeavour' of the calibre of Margaret Thatcher and Harold Wilson. 'In many ways, he sees the Middle East very similarly to Netanyahu,' Haaretz said, referring to current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who also held office from 2009 to 2021. Since last month, Netanyahu has repeatedly refused a ceasefire in Gaza and has promised to 'wipe Hamas off the face of the earth' in an aerial and ground offensive that has killed more than 11,200 Palestinians. During the 50 days of hostilities lasting from July 8 to August 26, 2014, 2,251 Palestinians were killed. Sayeeda Warsi, a senior minister in Britain's Foreign Office and Britain's first Muslim to serve in the cabinet, resigned as the ceasefire collapsed and accused Cameron's government of taking a 'morally indefensible' approach to the conflict. Warsi said at the time that the government's response to the events in Gaza was one of the factors behind the radicalisation of British Muslims, which could have consequences for years to come, citing early evidence from the Home Office. Yet, the member of the House of Lords appeared to have buried the hatchet as she welcomed Cameron back on Monday. 'If ever there was a time for balanced, thoughtful, compassionate leadership it is now. Your country needs you,' Warsi said on X. According to Whitham, the former prime minister's personal ties with Saudi Arabia have played a decisive role in his political reinstatement. Cameron was among a handful of leaders, including former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro and former US presidential senior adviser Jared Kushner, to travel to Saudi Arabia in 2019 for the 'Davos in the Desert' summit. 'We have [a pillar] in British foreign policy in the Middle East that is becoming more important in the post-Brexit context, which is ... that these foreign strategic allies outside of Europe, like Saudi Arabia, are really important,' Whitham said. 'Maintaining good relations with these partners comes above everything else,' he added. 'And Cameron is seen very much as a continuity candidate in this respect.' Cameron has been a supporter of using Britain's 'military prowess' to defeat groups regarded as 'terrorists' in the Middle East. In 2014, as ISIL (ISIS) sought to establish a 'caliphate' in Iraq and Syria, he warned that the West faced having an 'extremist' state on the borders of the Mediterranean if ISIL succeeded in its goals. His government agreed to extend air strikes into Syria from Iraq, where he voted in favour of an invasion when it was put to the British Parliament in March 2003. 'Probably the most controversial foreign policy decisions during Cameron's time as prime minister was the decision to use extrajudicial killings in Syria, which inaugurated a programme of drone strikes that continues to this day,' Whitham said. Since his resignation in 2016 after his unsuccessful bid for Britain to remain in the European Union, Cameron's Middle East policy has been reviewed and found to have had a lasting impact for the region. In 2011 when Britain and France intervened in Libya, Cameron's government said the operation was aimed at protecting civilians under fire from longtime leader Muammar Gaddafi. But the Foreign Affairs Committee later analysed the decision and found it had relied on flawed intelligence and hastened the North African country's political and economic collapse. The parliamentary report concluded that Cameron had a 'decisive' role in the decision to intervene and must bear the responsibility for Britain's role in the crisis in Libya. Much like former US President Barack Obama, Cameron opened the path to the use of lethal force in parts of the Middle East, Whitham said. 'Cameron has demonstrated that he's quite keen on military intervention in the region,' he said. 'I wouldn't want to speculate on whether he will join the chorus of pro-Israel voices and potentially frame Hamas as an extension of ISIS. That will be down to the line Sunak takes and Cameron will have to toe that line.'
translated_content: Der ehemalige Premierminister nannte Gaza ein 'Gefängnislager' und setzte sich für eine Zweistaatenlösung ein, ist aber auch ein standhafter Unterstützer Israels. Die unerwartete Rückkehr des ehemaligen britischen Premierministers David Cameron in die Politik während des Krieges in Gaza und der pro-palästinensischen Proteste in Großbritannien hat Fragen über die Implikationen für die britische Politik im Nahen Osten aufgeworfen. Cameron, nun Außenminister, hatte zuvor den Gazastreifen als 'Gefängnislager' bezeichnet und sich für eine Zweistaatenlösung im Israel-Palästina-Konflikt eingesetzt, ist aber auch ein standhafter Unterstützer Israels. Am 9. Oktober 2023, als Israel eine 'totale' Blockade von Gaza verkündete und das Gebiet als Vergeltung für einen Überraschungsangriff zwei Tage zuvor durch die bewaffnete palästinensische Gruppe Hamas bombardierte, machte der 57-Jährige seine Erklärung zugunsten Israels. 'Ich stehe in voller Solidarität mit Israel in dieser schwierigen Zeit und unterstütze den Premierminister und die britische Regierung in ihrer uneingeschränkten und standhaften Unterstützung', sagte er auf X und fügte die blau-weiße israelische Flagge in seinen Beitrag ein. 'Meine Gedanken und Gebete gelten dem Volk Israels nach den abscheulichen Terrorakten, die ihnen am Wochenende zugefügt wurden, und mein Herz gilt all jenen, die so grausam gegen ihren Willen verschleppt wurden, und ihren Familien. Ihre Sorge und ihr Herzschmerz sind einfach...' pic.twitter.com/yFkRIorHjs — David Cameron (@David_Cameron) 9. Oktober 2023. Hunderttausende Demonstranten marschierten am Wochenende in London aus Solidarität mit den Palästinensern in Gaza, während eine kleine Anzahl rechtsextremer Gruppen Gegendemonstrationen veranstaltete. Premierminister Rishi Sunak entließ Innenministerin Suella Braverman am Montag, nachdem sie die Polizei beschuldigt hatte, zu nachsichtig mit pro-palästinensischen Demonstranten umzugehen und Kommentare gemacht hatte, die als 'aufwiegelnd' beschrieben wurden. Er ersetzte Braverman durch Außenminister James Cleverly, bevor er Cameron als Cleverlys überraschenden Nachfolger bekannt gab. Ben Whitham, Professor für internationale Beziehungen an der School of Oriental and African Studies in London (SOAS), sagte, dass Cameron zwar einen 'versöhnlicheren Ton' anschlagen würde, aber nicht zugunsten der Palästinenser im Konflikt handeln würde. 'Sicherlich wird er, wie jeder hochrangige konservative Politiker, weitgehend auf der Seite Israels und seines angeblichen Rechts stehen, die Offensive in Gaza durchzuführen', sagte er gegenüber Al Jazeera. Whitham sagte, Camerons Ernennung ziele auch darauf ab, 'einige der Spaltungen innerhalb der Konservativen Partei zu heilen'. 'Er wird als jemand gesehen, der enge Beziehungen zu strategischen wirtschaftlichen Partnern im Nahen Osten hat', einschließlich einer andauernden persönlichen Beziehung zur Führung Saudi-Arabiens, sagte Whitham. Während seiner Amtszeit als Premierminister von 2010 bis 2016 kritisierte Cameron Israels 'illegale' Siedlungen im besetzten Westjordanland und die Blockade des Gazastreifens. 'Gaza darf nicht und kann nicht zu einem Gefängnislager werden', sagte er bei einem Besuch in der Türkei im Jahr 2010. Allerdings lehnte seine Partei die Forderungen von Koalitionsmitgliedern ab, die Waffenexportlizenzen nach Israel zu überprüfen, sollte der Kampf wieder aufgenommen werden, als die Palästinenser in Gaza von einem flüchtigen Waffenstillstand profitierten, der eines der tödlichsten Bombardements im Gazastreifen im Jahr 2014 vorübergehend stoppte. Die israelische Zeitung Haaretz zitierte die Episode als einen der Gründe, warum Cameron der pro-israelischste britische Premierminister aller Zeiten war und den Titel von 'glühenden' Unterstützern wie Gordon Brown und Tony Blair sowie 'unverhohlenen Bewunderern des zionistischen Unternehmens' wie Margaret Thatcher und Harold Wilson übernahm. 'In vielerlei Hinsicht sieht er den Nahen Osten sehr ähnlich wie Netanjahu', sagte Haaretz und bezog sich auf den derzeitigen Premierminister Benjamin Netanjahu, der auch von 2009 bis 2021 im Amt war. Seit letztem Monat hat Netanjahu wiederholt eine Waffenruhe in Gaza abgelehnt und versprochen, die Hamas 'vom Angesicht der Erde zu tilgen' in einer Luft- und Bodenoffensive, die mehr als 11.200 Palästinenser getötet hat. Während der 50 Tage andauernden Feindseligkeiten vom 8. Juli bis 26. August 2014 wurden 2.251 Palästinenser getötet. Sayeeda Warsi, eine hochrangige Ministerin im britischen Außenministerium und die erste Muslimin im Kabinett Großbritanniens, trat zurück, als der Waffenstillstand zusammenbrach, und warf der Regierung Cameron eine 'moralisch unvertretbare' Haltung im Konflikt vor. Warsi sagte damals, dass die Reaktion der Regierung auf die Ereignisse in Gaza einer der Faktoren für die Radikalisierung britischer Muslime sei, die jahrelange Folgen haben könnte, und berief sich auf frühe Beweise des Innenministeriums. Dennoch schien das Mitglied des Oberhauses den Streit beigelegt zu haben, als es Cameron am Montag willkommen hieß. 'Wenn es jemals eine Zeit für ausgewogene, nachdenkliche und mitfühlende Führung gab, dann jetzt. Dein Land braucht dich', sagte Warsi auf X. Laut Whitham spielten die persönlichen Beziehungen des ehemaligen Premierministers zu Saudi-Arabien eine entscheidende Rolle bei seiner politischen Wiedereinsetzung. Cameron gehörte zu einer Handvoll Führer, darunter der ehemalige brasilianische Präsident Jair Bolsonaro und der ehemalige senior Berater des US-Präsidenten, Jared Kushner, die 2019 zum 'Davos in der Wüste'-Gipfel nach Saudi-Arabien reisten. 'Wir haben [eine Säule] in der britischen Außenpolitik im Nahen Osten, die im post-Brexit-Kontext immer wichtiger wird, nämlich... dass diese strategischen Verbündeten außerhalb Europas, wie Saudi-Arabien, sehr wichtig sind', sagte Whitham. 'Die Aufrechterhaltung guter Beziehungen zu diesen Partnern steht über allem anderen', fügte er hinzu. 'Und Cameron wird sehr als Kontinuitätskandidat in dieser Hinsicht gesehen.' Cameron war ein Befürworter der Nutzung der britischen 'militärischen Stärke', um Gruppen zu besiegen, die im Nahen Osten als 'Terroristen' gelten. 2014 warnte er, als der IS (ISIS) versuchte, ein 'Kalifat' im Irak und in Syrien zu errichten, dass der Westen einem 'extremistischen' Staat an den Grenzen des Mittelmeers gegenüberstehen würde, wenn der IS erfolgreich wäre. Seine Regierung stimmte der Ausweitung der Luftangriffe von Irak nach Syrien zu, wo er 2003 für eine Invasion stimmte, als sie dem britischen Parlament vorgelegt wurde. 'Wahrscheinlich die umstrittenste außenpolitische Entscheidung während Camerons Amtszeit als Premierminister war die Entscheidung, außergerichtliche Tötungen in Syrien zu nutzen, was ein Programm von Drohnenangriffen einleitete, das bis heute andauert', sagte Whitham. Seit seinem Rücktritt 2016 nach seinem gescheiterten Versuch, Großbritannien in der Europäischen Union zu halten, wurde Camerons Nahostpolitik überprüft und festgestellt, dass sie bleibende Auswirkungen auf die Region hatte. 2011, als Großbritannien und Frankreich in Libyen intervenierten, sagte Camerons Regierung, die Operation ziele darauf ab, Zivilisten vor dem Beschuss des langjährigen Führers Muammar Gaddafi zu schützen. Aber das Außenpolitische Komitee analysierte die Entscheidung später und stellte fest, dass sie auf fehlerhaften Geheimdienstinformationen basierte und den politischen und wirtschaftlichen Zusammenbruch des nordafrikanischen Landes beschleunigte. Der parlamentarische Bericht kam zu dem Schluss, dass Cameron eine 'entscheidende' Rolle bei der Entscheidung zur Intervention gespielt habe und die Verantwortung für die Rolle Großbritanniens in der Krise in Libyen tragen müsse. Ähnlich wie der ehemalige US-Präsident Barack Obama ebnete Cameron den Weg für den Einsatz tödlicher Gewalt in Teilen des Nahen Ostens, sagte Whitham. 'Cameron hat gezeigt, dass er sehr an militärischen Interventionen in der Region interessiert ist', sagte er. 'Ich möchte nicht spekulieren, ob er sich dem Chor der pro-israelischen Stimmen anschließen und die Hamas potenziell als Verlängerung des IS darstellen wird. Das wird von der Linie abhängen, die Sunak einschlägt, und Cameron wird dieser Linie folgen müssen.'

article_content: In a tragic turn of events, at least 21 individuals were injured during the latest Pamplona bull run, with an Irishman suffering severe chest injuries. The horrifying scene unfolded live on Spanish television as a massive crowd crush occurred at the narrow entrance to the bullring. Officials reported that the bulls charged into a packed group of people, leading to a chaotic pile-up. As the powerful animals stormed into the tunnel entrance, they were met with a heap of fallen individuals, causing further panic and injury. One bull, after falling, charged back into the crowded passageway, while two steers leaped over the pile of people trying to escape. Several runners were trampled as the bulls attempted to climb over them. The Irishman is believed to have suffered asphyxiation due to his chest injury in the crush. The blockage was finally cleared when attendants guided the animals through a side door usually reserved for matadors. Javier Sesma, a health spokesman for Navarra province, confirmed that two out of the 21 injured were gored by bulls, with the rest suffering injuries from the stampede. A 19-year-old Spaniard from Vitoria city was critically injured when his thorax was crushed at the bullring entrance. Sesma described the situation as very grave but stable. Other injuries included a person gored in the buttock and another in the armpit during the 928-yard dash through Pamplona's narrow streets. The Navarra government, which organizes the annual festivities, reported that the rest of the injured had cuts and bruises, and one spectator suffered a heart attack while watching. The festival gained global attention on Friday when an American college student, Patrick Eccles, and two Spaniards were gored, with videos and photos of the attacks circulating worldwide. Each morning, six fighting bulls and six steers are released from stables to the bullring for afternoon bullfights. The last fatal goring occurred in 2009, and the festivities conclude today.
translated_content: In einer tragischen Wendung der Ereignisse wurden beim jüngsten Stierlauf in Pamplona mindestens 21 Personen verletzt, darunter ein Ire mit schweren Brustverletzungen. Die schockierende Szene spielte sich live im spanischen Fernsehen ab, als es zu einem Massengedränge am schmalen Eingang zur Stierkampfarena kam. Beamte berichteten, dass die Stiere in eine dichte Menschenmenge stürmten, was zu einem chaotischen Durcheinander führte. Als die mächtigen Tiere in den Tunneleingang stürmten, trafen sie auf einen Haufen gestürzter Menschen, was weitere Panik und Verletzungen verursachte. Ein Stier, der gestürzt war, stürmte zurück in den überfüllten Durchgang, während zwei Ochsen über den Haufen von Menschen sprangen, die zu fliehen versuchten. Mehrere Läufer wurden niedergetrampelt, als die Stiere versuchten, über sie hinwegzuklettern. Man geht davon aus, dass der Ire aufgrund seiner Brustverletzung im Gedränge erstickt ist. Die Blockade wurde schließlich geräumt, als Ordner die Tiere durch eine Seitentür führten, die normalerweise für Matadore reserviert ist. Javier Sesma, ein Gesundheitssprecher der Provinz Navarra, bestätigte, dass zwei der 21 Verletzten von Stieren aufgespießt wurden, während die anderen bei der Stampede verletzt wurden. Ein 19-jähriger Spanier aus Vitoria wurde schwer verletzt, als sein Brustkorb am Eingang der Stierkampfarena zerquetscht wurde. Sesma beschrieb die Situation als sehr ernst, aber stabil. Weitere Verletzungen umfassten eine Person, die in das Gesäß gestochen wurde, und eine andere, die in die Achselhöhle gestochen wurde, während des 928 Meter langen Laufs durch die engen Straßen Pamplonas. Die Regierung von Navarra, die die jährlichen Festlichkeiten organisiert, berichtete, dass die restlichen Verletzten Schnitte und Prellungen hatten und ein Zuschauer einen Herzinfarkt erlitt, während er zusah. Das Festival erlangte weltweite Aufmerksamkeit, als am Freitag ein amerikanischer College-Student, Patrick Eccles, und zwei Spanier aufgespießt wurden, wobei Videos und Fotos der Angriffe weltweit kursierten. Jeden Morgen werden sechs Kampfstiere und seix Ochsen aus den Ställen zur Stierkampfarena für die Nachmittags-Stierkämpfe freigelassen. Die letzte tödliche Verletzung durch einen Stier ereignete sich 2009, und die Festlichkeiten enden heute.

article_content: Princess Maxima, who will become Queen of Holland following her mother-in-law's abdication, bears a striking resemblance to pop sensation Britney Spears, according to internet observers. Maxima Zorreguieta, the wife of Willem-Alexander, who will be King Willem-Alexander, has been compared to the 31-year-old pop singer, who rose to fame in 1999 and has since faced a failed marriage and several controversies. Gawker user EbenHJ agreed with the comparison, stating: 'Yeah, except I'm going to go out on a limb and guess that she wears underwear and has never gotten married in Las Vegas for 72 hours and then shaved her head. Other than that, they could totally be the same person.' Mirror image: Princess Maxima of The Netherlands' (right) appearance has been compared to that of pop star Britney Spears (left). The resemblance is uncanny, despite a 10-year age gap. Jamie Beck on entertainment website Crushable also noted the uncanny resemblance, saying: 'I guess you could blame the tanned, flaxen-haired beauty myth that they are both trying to resemble, ingrained as it is in the consciousness of so many. They have the same bad dye/extensions job, the same heavy eye makeup, and the same vague look that something isn’t right.' Princess Maxima, 40, has been in the spotlight ever since the Netherlands' reigning queen, Beatrix, who turns 75 on January 31st, announced on Monday that she would abdicate the throne to her son this spring, so that the crown could pass to 'a new generation'. Wave 4 U: Britney acknowledges her fans, while Princess Maxima greets her subjects. Hats off: Despite the resemblance, the two widely-known women have had very different lives. Marriages: Princess Maxima and Prince Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands... and Britney with ex-husband Kevin Federline in 2005. Princess Maxima was born a commoner in Argentina and is the daughter of a minister who served in the military junta in the late 1970s. The royal couple have three daughters, Amalia, nine, Alexia, seven, and Ariane, five. Britney Spears was born in Mississippi and raised in Kentwood, Louisiana. She performed on stage and in television shows as a child before her first album ...Baby One More Time achieved wild success. She has two children and recently split from former fiancé Jason Trawick.

PUBLISHED: 17:43 EST, 2 January 2014 | UPDATED: 19:55 EST, 2 January 2014 Police caught a presumed dead Georgia banker this week in a routine traffic stop, after he went off the grid almost two years ago following a $20 million fraud scheme. Aubrey Lee Price, 47, made his first appearance in court today in Brunswick, Georgia, after his arrest on Tuesday. He is being tried for one count of bank fraud and if found guilty could spend 30 years in prison and face a maximum fine of $1,000,000. The FBI had been searching for Price ever since June 2012 when he sent a suicide letter to his family, saying he planned to take a ferry to Key West and jump into the ocean to end his life. In court: Aubrey Lee Price, who was caught on Tuesday after 18 months on the run, appeared in court today. Caught: Price, who will return to court for a bail hearing on Monday, allegedly faked his suicide to avoid charges. Price disappeared on June 16, 2012, after telling his family he was going to Guatemala on a business trip, authorities said. Two days later, his family and acquaintances received letters from him detailing his plot to jump off the ferry. 'My depression and discouragement have driven me to deep anxiety, fear, and shame. I am emotionally overwhelmed and incapable of continuing in this life,' said a rambling confession letter investigators believe was written by Price. 'I created false statements, covered up my losses, and deceived and hurt the very people I was trying to help,' the letter said. It seemed that Price had followed through with the plan when credit card records showed he bought dive weights and a ferry ticket. Price was captured on surveillance footage at the Key West airport and ferry terminal the day he disappeared, and the ferry ticket was scanned at the boarding point. Those letters prompted a U.S. Coast Guard search for Price, which cost $173,000. Back from the dead: Former bank director Aubrey Lee Price was caught by police after he had been missing since June 2012, when he had told family members he was going to commit suicide. More than a year ago, a Florida judge declared Price to be legally dead, but the FBI continued to search for him, offering a reward of up to $20,000 for his capture. Price disappeared in June 2012 after sending a rambling letter to his family and acquaintances that investigators described as a confession. The FBI turned out to be right when police in Glynn County, Georgia, stopped him for a tinted window violation on Interstate 95. Officers said that it was clear Price was giving them false information during the stop and they were soon able to determine that he was wanted by the FBI. After his capture, Price told authorities that since disappearing he had been working as a migrant worker, accepting cash for odd jobs. At his appearance in court today, Price sported long, unkempt hair and a straggly beard, a far cry from his neat, suited appearance two years ago. Back then, Price was the director of Montgomery Bank & Trust in Ailey, Georgia, at the time of his disappearance. In December 2010, when a company he controlled bought a controlling portion of the bank's stock, according to a complaint filed in June 2012 in federal court in New York. article_content: By Daniel Bates. PUBLISHED: 11:21 EST, 6 May 2013. UPDATED: 11:21 EST, 6 May 2013. A British pub in New York is facing a human rights prosecution and a £5,000 fine after advertising for bar staff who are from the UK. The Longbow Pub and Pantry was accused of discrimination because the advert stated that ‘being British definitely works in your favor’. Its owners also claimed that staff had to know why Liverpool v Everton is an important match, and that the Old Firm refers to a match between Celtic and Rangers and not a law company. 'Being British definitely works in your favor': The Longbow Pub and Pantry in Brooklyn, New York, added that statement to a vacancy for bar staff advertised on the classified ads website Craigslist. The New York City Commission on Human Rights disagreed and said its administrative code bans adverts which demand that staff be a specific nationality. It has set up a ‘conciliation meeting’ for talks with the pub’s owners, Jennifer and Michael Colbert, but unless a deal is reached, there will be a trial with a fine of up to £5,000. Mrs. Colbert is from Brooklyn, New York, but considers herself an honorary Brit as her husband of 19 years, Mr. Colbert, a carpenter, is from Wrexham. They posted the advert to the online classifieds website Craigslist after hiring somebody who did not know British culture. Mrs. Colbert said: ‘She was from (New) Jersey. The customers didn’t take to her. She didn’t understand when they were making jokes. There’s a certain cadence to the sarcasm that just flew over her shoulders’. After asking her to leave, they wrote the advert which read that they wanted ‘energetic and enthusiastic men and women with an appreciation of craft beer, good food, whiskey, and real football (a.k.a. soccer). Being British definitely works in your favor’. Mr. Colbert and his wife have vowed to fight the claims they are discriminating and wrote a letter to the commission outlining their case. It read that staff working in their pub had to know that ‘knocking someone up’ is not about being pregnant as it does in the U.S., and that a banger had nothing to do with gangs, as in the American phrase ‘gang banger’. Another issue was that Americans think that black pudding is a dessert, they wrote. Cliff Mulqueen, the general counsel for the New York City Commission on Human Rights, said that the Colberts were ‘missing the point’. He told the New York Times: ‘There’s an argument that someone who works in a Chinese restaurant, for example, may need to speak Chinese in order to communicate with their co-workers. But there’s a difference between saying you have to speak Chinese and saying you have to be Chinese’.

article_content: In a disturbing incident, an Indiana woman named Jessica Clark has been sentenced to six months in prison. Her crime? Allowing her 7-year-old daughter to be tied to the hood of a car driven by her intoxicated boyfriend, Aaron Stefanski. Just days earlier, Stefanski himself was sentenced to 18 months of home detention for his reckless actions. Clark, who is 30 years old, received a total sentence of two and a half years, but two years of that were suspended and will be served on probation. The first six months of her probation will be under home detention. The shocking event unfolded in Fort Wayne, where Stefanski, 29, was found to have a blood alcohol level of 0.17 percent—more than double the legal limit. He had tied his own three young children and Clark's daughter to the hood of his car, claiming he thought they would enjoy it. Despite the severity of his actions, Stefanski expressed remorse in court, stating that alcohol clouded his judgment. He has since been addressing his alcohol problem and taking parenting classes. The judge overseeing the case, Superior Judge Wendy Davis, described the situation as 'incredibly aggravating' and emphasized the importance of protecting children. Stefanski has been barred from seeing his children since the incident.

article_content: Google is facing a growing backlash over its 'Glass' eyewear, with café owners in the US banning the technology from their premises. Dave Meinert, who runs the 5 Point Café in Seattle, said those wearing the spectacles will have to remove them if they want to come in. He has put up a sign on the wall which reads: 'Respect our customers’ privacy as we’d expect them to respect yours.' Invasion of privacy?: Google Glass can film what the wearer sees without any indication to others. The move comes after it emerged that people wearing Google Glass could be banned from American cinemas, casinos, and even parks because owners don’t want filming there. The glasses, which cost $1,500 a pair (£980), are currently on limited release to 2,000 customers but will be more widely available later this year. Should Google Glass be banned in cafés to protect customers' privacy? A camera next to the wearer’s eye, which can take photos or record video without a red light or a shutter sound to tell others that it is working, has caused concerns for privacy. Casinos said the futuristic eyewear could help cheaters to win unfairly and cinemas said they could be used to illegally record films and sell pirate copies. Lap dance clubs said that they would treat those wearing the Internet-connected specs the same as anyone caught filming a stripper with a cameraphone—and would kick them out. Behind the lens: Wearers of Google Glass can film as they walk around wearing the technology. Parks departments and banks across America are also waiting to see how the new technology is used before deciding whether or not to ban them. Dan Tench, of legal firm Olswang, which is coordinating a privacy lawsuit against Google in the UK, said: 'This is the ultimate snooper’s gizmo. If you walk around with a video camera filming, it’s obvious what you’re doing, but with Google Glass, it’s much, much more invasive.' Google’s chairman Eric Schmidt once admitted that the aim with such technology was to 'go right up to the creepy line and not cross it.' But the public clearly feels differently and in France those wearing Google Glass style specs have been subjected to 'cyber discrimination.' University of Toronto computer engineering professor Steve Mann was at a McDonald’s restaurant in Paris when he claims an employee tried to physically remove a similar gadget he designed from his head.

article_content: (CNN) -- The French Open semifinal between Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic, touted by many as the real final, lived up to its billing. After an intense battle lasting over four and a half hours on a scorching day in Paris, Nadal emerged victorious. The defending champion is now one match away from securing a record-extending eighth French Open title, having defeated the world No. 1 with a score of 6-4, 3-6, 6-1, 6-7, 9-7. 'I was ready for the fight,' Nadal told reporters. Nadal is now the heavy favorite to defeat fourth-seed David Ferrer in Sunday's all-Spanish final. Ferrer, who easily beat Frenchman Jo-Wilfried Tsonga 6-1, 7-6(3), 6-2 in the other semifinal, will be competing in his first grand slam final and has lost 16 consecutive matches on clay against Nadal. In their 35th meeting, Nadal improved his record against Djokovic to 5-0 at the French Open. For a while, it seemed Djokovic might continue his winning streak against Nadal, having beaten him in three straight grand slam finals since 2011, including a six-hour marathon in the 2012 Australian Open final. Djokovic led 4-2 in the fifth set after Nadal squandered a break lead in the second and couldn't close out the match in the fourth. It was only the second time Nadal has been pushed to five sets at Roland Garros. 'When I was serving for the match, it was against the wind, so I knew it would be tough,' Nadal said. 'It was similar to the match in Australia in 2012, and he won. This time, I won, and that's what makes sport so exciting.' The match wasn't without controversy. With Djokovic leading 4-3 in the fifth and at deuce, he executed a simple smash. However, chair umpire Pascal Maria ruled that Djokovic touched the net before the ball bounced twice, awarding the point to Nadal. Djokovic won the next point to revert to deuce but eventually lost the game, allowing Nadal to break for 4-4. 'Who knows what direction the match may have taken if I had won that point,' Djokovic told reporters. 'On 99.9 percent of other occasions, I would have got the point.' Maria had earlier given both players warnings for taking too much time between points. Djokovic was also upset that his request to water the court in the fifth set was denied, feeling the court was too dry and slippery. Nadal started strong, taking control of the first set in the hot conditions that suited his heavy ground strokes. With Djokovic making errors and Nadal hitting deep, the Spaniard broke for 4-3 and won the first set. He seemed poised for victory after breaking again for 3-2 in the second set. However, Nadal dropped his serve in the following game, losing four games in a row and leveling the match. Nadal dominated the third set and led again in the fourth, breaking for 4-3 only to drop serve for 4-4. Uncharacteristically, Nadal couldn't close out the match when serving at 6-5. As Nadal hit shorter, Djokovic stepped in to crush his ground strokes. A struggling Nadal was broken to start the fifth set but rallied, aided by Djokovic's errors on several overheads. 'It's a very special win for me, and congratulations to Novak,' Nadal said. 'He's a great champion and will win here at Roland Garros one day.' Ferrer capitalized on Tsonga's apparent nerves in the first set and overcame a 3-0 deficit in the second. Once Ferrer won the second set, Tsonga's performance declined. Tsonga was aiming to become the first Frenchman in 30 years to win a major.

Der Stuhlschiedsrichter Pascal Maria entschied jedoch, dass Djokovic das Netz berührt hatte, bevor der Ball zweimal aufsprang, und gab den Punkt an Nadal. Djokovic gewann den nächsten Punkt, um wieder Einstand zu erreichen, verlor aber schließlich das Spiel, was Nadal den Break zum 4-4 ermöglichte. 'Wer weiß, in welche Richtung das Spiel gegangen wäre, wenn ich diesen Punkt gewonnen hätte', sagte Djokovic gegenüber Reportern. 'Bei 99,9 Prozent anderer Gelegenheiten hätte ich den Punkt bekommen.' Maria hatte beiden Spielern zuvor eine Verwarnung wegen Zeitüberschreitung zwischen den Punkten gegeben. Djokovic war auch verärgert, dass sein Antrag, den Platz im fünften Satz zu bewässern, abgelehnt wurde, da er den Platz als zu trocken und rutschig empfand. Nadal startete stark und übernahm die Kontrolle im ersten Satz bei heißen Bedingungen, die seinen schweren Grundschlägen entgegenkamen. Als Djokovic Fehler machte und Nadal tief schlug, breakte der Spanier zum 4-3 und gewann den ersten Satz. Er schien auf dem Weg zum Sieg, nachdem er im zweiten Satz erneut zum 3-2 gebreakt hatte. Nadal verlor jedoch seinen Aufschlag im folgenden Spiel, verlor vier Spiele in Folge und glich das Match aus. Nadal dominierte den dritten Satz und führte erneut im vierten, brach zum 4-3, nur um den Aufschlag zum 4-4 zu verlieren. Untypischerweise konnte Nadal das Match nicht beenden, als er beim Stand von 6-5 aufschlug. Als Nadal kürzer schlug, trat Djokovic vor, um seine Grundschläge zu zertrümmern. Ein kämpfender Nadal wurde zu Beginn des fünften Satzes gebreakt, fand aber wieder ins Spiel, unterstützt durch Djokovic's Fehler bei mehreren Overheads. 'Es ist ein sehr besonderer Sieg für mich, und herzlichen Glückwunsch an Novak', sagte Nadal. 'Er ist ein großer Champion und wird eines Tages hier bei Roland Garros gewinnen.' Ferrer nutzte Tsonga's offensichtliche Nervosität im ersten Satz und drehte einen 0-3-Rückstand im zweiten Satz. Sobald Ferrer den zweiten Satz gewonnen hatte, ließ Tsonga's Leistung nach. Tsonga hatte das Ziel, der erste Franzose seit 30 Jahren zu werden, der ein Major gewinnt.
